entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:2
segments: Is gone down into his garden; the spouse in union with her beloved is herself "a garden inclosed," full of the precious fruits of righteousness.
Or, she stands in the midst of her garden and calls her beloved to partake of its fruits.

But, in leaving her beloved, she has left the heavenly garden also, and there she must seek him again. 
 
Christ dwells in his garden amid the fruits of holiness; and they who seek him there shall find him.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:3
segments:
I am my beloved's; the separation is now ended, and in the following verses the bridegroom sets forth the excellences of his bride. 
 
Christ's love for his people remains strong even in their departure from him; and when they return to him with all their heart, he will graciously receive them, and restore them to their former union and communion with himself.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:4
segments: Tirzah; a pleasant city, for a time the capital of the kingdom of Israel.
Terrible as an army with banners; see note on

. 
 
vv 4-10. 
 
However men may despise Christ's church, she is most precious in his eyes, and he will make her, by the gifts of his Spirit, "fair as the moon, clear as the sun," and to all her enemies, "terrible as an army with banners."

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:8
segments: , the queen is represented as preeminent above all her attendants.  In the spiritual application, the words mean, that "the bride, the Lamb's wife," is loved and honored by all her members.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:11
segments: I went down; this is probably the beginning of a new representation.  The bridegroom has gone down into his garden, as in
.  There he is seized with longing affection for his absent spouse, and calls upon her to return, that he may behold her beauty.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:12
segments: Like the chariots of Amminadib; or, "the chariots of my willing people."  In either case, the reference is to return, that he may behold her beauty.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:13
segments:
Return, O Shulamite; Shulamite seems to be a symbolic name of the bride, having a designed resemblance to that of Solomon, who represents the heavenly Bridegroom, in both form and meaning.  This is more manifest in the Hebrew, thus: 
 
  Shelomoh, Solomon, that is, the Peaceful,

. 
 
  What will ye see; the words of the spouse, expressing a sense of her unworthiness. 
 
  As it were the company of two armies; or, "As it were the dances of Mahanaim;" that is, the exulting bands of angels that met Jacob on his return from Padanaram.

.  This is the response of the bridegroom.  Mahanaim means, two hosts. 
 
When the believer has the deepest sense of his unworthiness, he is most excellent and honorable in the sight of God.
